The three-dimensional ultrasound-validated large-core needle biopsy (3D ultrasound LCNB) is considered a reliable method for the histological assessment of breast lesions. This technique provides high-quality images that can help accurately identify the type of lesion, its location, and any potential features such as margins or invasion.

In fact, studies have shown that 3D ultrasound validation of the postfire needle position is an efficient adjunct to ultrasound-guided LCNB. By using 3D ultrasound to verify the accurate placement of the needle, healthcare professionals can reduce the need for multiple core samples and minimize the risk of tumor cell displacement.

The advantages of 3D ultrasound validation include a reduction in the number of core samples needed, shorter procedure times, lower costs, and improved diagnostic accuracy. Additionally, 3D ultrasound validation allows for better evaluation of complex lesions and can help identify features that may be missed by other imaging modalities.

In summary, the use of 3D ultrasound-validated large-core needle biopsy is a reliable method for the histological assessment of breast lesions, offering several benefits over traditional methods.
